basic_info.name: PupuJEPA (Frequency-Aware Self-Supervised Music Representation Learning)
basic_info.org: Yicheng Gu, Junan Zhang, Jerry Li, Zhizheng Wu, Lauri Juvela — Spellbrush, Aalto University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
basic_info.release_date: arXiv preprint June 2026 (arXiv:2606.25713); submitted to IEEE TASLP; codes and checkpoints available at project page https://www.yichenggu.com/PupuJEPA/
basic_info.links: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25713; Project page (code + checkpoints): https://www.yichenggu.com/PupuJEPA/; HuggingFace paper page: https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.25713

architecture.backbone: Visual Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA): context encoder + target encoder + predictor, all standard Vision Transformers (ViTs) operating directly on 2D Mel-spectrogram patches. PupuJEPA-Tiny variant has ~5M parameters. Domain-specific modifications: target encoder restricted to only target patches (prevents shortcut learning/collapse on spectrograms), blockwise and time-frequency masking instead of random masking, and 2D-aware layer fusion (learnable weighted sum across layers or MLP reduce after patch-wise pooling) plus time/frequency/block-partitioned patch aggregation replacing global average pooling.
architecture.training_objective: Masked latent prediction (JEPA-style, no masking-prediction-in-token-space): predict latent embeddings of masked 2D spectrogram patches from unmasked contexts via the predictor; target encoder is EMA-style self-distillation as in standard JEPAs (I-JEPA/V-JEPA family). Not contrastive, not MAE reconstruction, not DINO (paper explicitly rejects MAE and DINO for music). The task summary's claim of 'without masking prediction' is interpreted as: no token-level masked-language-modeling prediction target — prediction happens in latent embedding space only [uncertain].
architecture.embedding_output: Global embeddings for downstream probing built from multi-layer 2D patch features H ∈ R^(L×T×F×D): patch-wise average pooling along hidden dim, learnable weighted-sum layer fusion (or MLP reduce), then time-/frequency-/block-partitioned patch aggregation with flattening and concatenation instead of GAP. Exact final embedding dim per checkpoint not clearly stated [uncertain].

data.training_data: Trained on an in-house (proprietary Spellbrush) music dataset; scale, sources, and license not disclosed in the paper abstract/project page [uncertain]. General-audio SSL baselines (AudioMAE++, MATPAC++, A-JEPA) were retrained on the same in-house data for fair comparison; music SSL baselines (MERT, Dasheng, MuQ, MusicFM) used official MARBLE checkpoints.

performance.benchmarks: Evaluated on the MARBLE benchmark (music/audio SSL embedding-family evaluation suite) with linear probing: outperforms 1D sequence-based SSL models (MERT, Dasheng, MuQ, MusicFM) and 2D spectrogram audio SSL baselines (AudioMAE++, MATPAC++, A-JEPA) across multiple MIR tasks. Especially strong on tasks addressable from spectrograms (e.g., GS key detection, where PupuJEPA-Tiny at 5M params beats almost all baselines). No MuChoMusic/MusicBench/SongDescriber/LLM-family numbers reported. Exact per-task MARBLE scores not captured here [uncertain].
performance.vs_clap: No direct head-to-head vs LAION-CLAP/MuLan reported; CLAP is not in the MARBLE linear-probing comparison set. Comparison is against MuQ/MusicFM/MERT/Dasheng SSL encoders, where PupuJEPA is claimed SOTA [uncertain on any indirect CLAP delta].

availability.license: Not explicitly stated on project page or abstract [uncertain]. Code and checkpoints are publicly released (project page); paper submitted to TASLP. License of checkpoints and of the in-house training data is unknown.

fit_for_local_playlist.sample_rate: Not explicitly documented in the sources reviewed [uncertain]; spectrogram-based ViT models in this family commonly use 16–24 kHz; repo standard is 48k mono so resampling would be required.
fit_for_local_playlist.inference_cost: PupuJEPA-Tiny is ~5M parameters (beats most MARBLE baselines on GS key detection); larger ViT variants exist but exact parameter counts are not captured here [uncertain]. ViT on spectrograms is CPU-feasible for the tiny variant; no per-track latency figures published.
fit_for_local_playlist.full_track_context: Trained/inferred on spectrogram patches; inference paradigm aggregates over the full 2D time-frequency grid of the input, but documented input window length (e.g., 10s vs multi-minute) is not stated [uncertain]. Long multi-minute tracks would need windowing with the described partitioned aggregation.
fit_for_local_playlist.frame_level_support: Yes, structurally: the model produces per-patch (time × frequency position) features before aggregation, and time-/frequency-/block-partitioned aggregation explicitly preserves time-frequency layout — a natural fit for section-level logic, but the paper does not ship a frame-level embedding API [uncertain on usability].
fit_for_local_playlist.multilingual_queries: No text interface at all — audio-only SSL encoder (no text tower, no joint space). Any text query would need a separately trained projection/retrieval head.
fit_for_local_playlist.retrieval_steering: None built in. Audio-only representation model; steering would require external tooling (e.g., the Sparse Steerable Retrieval approach applied on top of embeddings).
